newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - FRN for Indonesia's BDN.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - FRN for Indonesia's BDN.

text.p: Indonesian state bank Bank Dagang Negara launched a US$95 million floating rate note issue into Asian debt markets on Wednesday.
The deal is only the second for an Indonesian state bank this year and bankers said they don't expect much more action from the banks until early in 1997.
The FRN matures in seven years but can be put or called after five. It was priced and re-offered at par to float at 67 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return is 72 basis points.
Daiwa Securities Hong Kong and HSBC Markets are joint leads and bookrunners.
Bank Dagang Negara last tapped the capital markets in November of 1995 with a 10-year, seven-year put US$180 million FRN, which was led by Merrill Lynch.
That six-year paper now is trading at about 80-82 basis points in the secondary market.
Some bankers complained that the pricing on the latest issue is too tight, saying they would be happier with an all-in of 75-76 basis points over the benchmark.

But a syndicate manager at HSBC Markets said the pricing was reasonable given where other Indonesian state banks are trading in the secondary market and in light of the price talk on other possible state bank deals.
Bank Rakyat, for example, is looking to pay 75 basis points for five years for its next transaction, he said.
Moreover, "Indonesian (secondary market) spreads have tightened in the last few weeks after widening after the riots," he said.
Political disturbances in Indonesia over the summer temporarily rattled the country's financial markets.
The leads kept more than 50 percent of the issue. A diverse group of banks took the rest.

JP Morgan Securities Asia joined as a senior co-lead manager. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Merrill Lynch took part as co-leads, while Asahi Finance Hong Kong, BW Bank, BZW, Chase Manhattan Asia, DKB Asia, IBJ Asia, Painwebber and Sakura Merchant Bank Singapore joined as co-managers.
Bank of Taiwan, the island's top state-run bank, came through late in the Asian day with its long-awaited US$200 million five-year floating rate note.
The notes pay a margin of LIBOR plus 1/16. Fees are eight basis points.
In other news, Hong Kong's Dah Sing Bank raised its three-year floating rate certificates of deposit issue to HK$1.5 billion from HK$1.2 billion due to oversubscription in syndication.
